answer: Churn is counted in beacon, and nebula publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 19% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. An hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the jade history. A 241 account operation therefore ties up 9 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
